description: §19.16.2 (S432 B3) — `return` fixes WHICH value is returned before the deferred bodies run, but does not freeze that value's contents: mk() returns { o, arr } and its deferred `o.a = 2` / `arr.push(9)` run after the return value is built, on the same objects the caller receives. trace = "2;2;" (as in Go, where a deferred mutation of a returned pointer's target is visible).
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S439 #6 (the four defer SPEC calls, all recs)
rationale: §19.16.2 Exit: `return` runs the deferred bodies after the return value has been evaluated; the deferred body cannot rebind what is returned, but an object or array the returned value references is the same object afterwards, so a deferred mutation of it is observable by the caller.
